title: SLA drift: prefetch pacing causing TTFT and tokens/sec degradation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Priya Singh
description: Several enterprise customers (hosted/dedicated/private) reported sustained TTFT regressions and ~30-40% drop in tokens/sec for long-context and multi-model fanout requests. Root cause appears correlated with a recent prefetch pacing heuristic change that interacts poorly with the per-tenant warmup credit allocator and KV-cache eviction thresholds. Symptoms include increased first-token latency for multiplexed sessions, slow token emission after warmstart, and periodic drops in throughput when cross-tenant warmup credits are exhausted.
steps_taken: Reproduced issue against staging using customer trace replay (trace IDs provided in links).
Added high-cardinality timing spans around prefetch call, kv-load, scheduler enqueue/dequeue, and kernel selection (deployed quick-change instrumentation).
Rolled prefetch pacing config back for one dedicated pool as litmus test (observed immediate TTFT improvement).
Scoped affected host pools by comparing kernel selection rates, warmup-credit consumption, and eviction counts across regions.
observations: TTFT regressed from median ~120ms to ~420ms on affected requests (measured on rwd-3b-int8 and rwx-13b-fp16 variants).
Tokens/sec for sustained streams dropped 30-38% when prefetch pacing triggered concurrent warmups across >4 models in a single tenant session.
KV-cache eviction rate rose ~2.7x after pacing change; evidence of thrashing when warmup credits shifted between workers.
Scheduler logs show bursts of 'prefetch-blocked' events that coincide with ENQUEUE latency spikes.
proposed_fixes: Introduce backpressure-aware prefetch gate: only prefetch when per-tenant warmup credits > threshold.
Adjust kv-cache soft-eviction threshold to prioritize recent token prefixes for multiplex sessions.
Telemetry-only A/B: enable new pacing heuristic for 5% of traffic with fine-grained metrics (TTFT, tokens/sec, eviction_count).
Short-term config rollback for hosted pools where customers are escalated (manual rollout via ops).
Add fast-path that bypasses prefetch for short (<=64) context primes to reduce unnecessary warmups.
planned_work: Today: ship telemetry roll with prefetch gating flag and a conservative threshold; monitor customer lanes for improvements.
48h: implement kv-cache soft-eviction tweak + add unit/integration tests for warmup-credit accounting.
72h: run controlled canary on dedicated and private deployments with metric-based roll/rollback automation.
Next sprint: refactor warmup-credit allocator to separate cross-tenant vs per-tenant budgets and add fairness limiter.
risks: Over-aggressive prefetch disabling risks small regressions in cold-start latency for low-concurrency workloads.
Tweaking eviction thresholds could increase memory usage on hosts with high long-context churn.
Rollback of config may hide root scheduling issues; work could recur without addressing allocator fairness.
rollback_plan: If any customer SLA metric (TTFT median or tokens/sec) for the canary or escalated pools worsens by >10% within 60m after change, immediately revert prefetch gating flag and restore previous kv-cache thresholds; notify on-call, PM, and customer success. Maintain a one-click rollback runbook in runbooks/latency-prefetch-rollback.md.
notes: PM (Daniel Park) joined triage and authorized P0 rollback for two hosted pools; CS notified enterprise contacts.
Design suggested UX banner for customers on Dedicated offering affected by throughput degradation to set expectations.
Follow-up: schedule postmortem with cross-functional attendees and add test coverage for multi-model warmup scenarios.
